business_scope.primary_industry_name: Trailing Suction Hopper Dredging and Rubble Mound Breakwater Works

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No specific bilateral investment treaty or double taxation agreement can be conclusively identified without the investor's country of residence or incorporation.
Spain is a party to numerous bilateral investment treaties and double taxation agreements; applicability depends on the investor's nationality, residence, ownership chain, and treaty qualification.

Treaty and EU-law framework potentially relevant to qualifying investors includes the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, applicable EU freedom-of-establishment and capital-movement rules, and the applicable Spain treaty network.
The Energy Charter Treaty should not be assumed to apply to a new investment because Spain notified withdrawal from the treaty, with effect subject to the treaty withdrawal framework.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving its implementing regulation; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales); Spanish Companies Act, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July; applicable EU AML legislation, EU financial-sanctions regulations, and Law 12/2003 of 21 May on the prevention and blocking of terrorist financing.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Apply customer and beneficial-owner identification, ownership-and-control verification, purpose-of-business analysis, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth review, and ongoing monitoring under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014. Screen all relevant persons and entities against United Nations and European Union sanctions lists and applicable Spanish measures. OFAC screening is not generally a Spanish statutory requirement but is prudent for U.S.-linked persons, U.S.-dollar clearing, U.S. financial institutions, and correspondent-bank exposure. Apply enhanced due diligence for PEPs, family members, close associates, opaque chains, high-risk jurisdictions, state-linked counterparties, unusual maritime payments, cash exposure, and port or public-procurement relationships. Obtain senior-management approval for PEP relationships and document risk-based monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central official portal: https://www.rmc.es; electronic filing and incorporation channels may also include the Colegio de Registradores portal and CIRCE through https://paeelectronico.es.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in an accepted form for the Spanish Commercial Registry and must include the legal-form designation or abbreviation, such as Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada or S.L. The name must be sufficiently distinctive, must not create confusion with an existing registered or reserved name, and must not be misleading or contrary to law, public order, or public interest. Spanish, co-official regional languages, and Latin-script names may be accepted subject to registry review. Foreign-language or transliterated names should be accompanied by a clear corporate-purpose description and may be rejected if misleading or insufficiently distinctive. The company name is separate from any trademark clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government, ministry, secretariat, municipality, state, national, official, royal, crown, royal house, embassy, consulate, diplomatic, European Union, European, bank, banking, credit, savings, insurance, securities, stock exchange, investment, finance, financial, fund, mutual, cooperative credit, airport, port authority, police, military, armed forces, university, chamber of commerce, and other terms implying public authority or regulated financial, insurance, educational, transport, or governmental activity.
Sensitive terms generally require supporting authorization, a lawful corporate purpose, or prior clearance from the competent authority rather than automatic approval.
Names identical or confusingly similar to existing names, trademarks, public institutions, or regulated entities are prohibited or likely to be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Apply to the Registro Mercantil Central for a certificate of non-coincidence before execution of the incorporation deed. The certificate is generally valid for three months from issuance for notarial incorporation purposes, while the approved name is generally reserved for six months. If rejected, obtain the stated registry defect, compare the proposed name against the Commercial Registry and trademark databases, and submit a corrected application or a reasoned administrative challenge to the Registro Mercantil Central within the applicable procedural period. A registrar decision may be challenged through the Commercial Registry appeal system before the Directorate-General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith, with subsequent judicial review before the competent courts where legally available. A rejection appeal does not cure an identical-name or misleading-name defect; changing the name is usually faster.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish S.L. must have a registered office in Spain under Article 9 of the Spanish Companies Act. A virtual office may be acceptable for receiving correspondence and maintaining a registered address if the provider permits legal service and the address is genuine and registrable. It is not adequate as the sole operational substance for marine dredging, seawall construction, EPC contracting, port-authority work, equipment storage, environmental compliance, occupational safety, customs, or public procurement. The company should maintain demonstrable management, accounting, banking, contract administration, technical personnel, equipment access, and project records in appropriate locations. Sectoral permits, port concessions, environmental approvals, contractor classifications, and site-specific authorizations remain separate requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 25-50% annual risk of an unannounced or short-notice physical verification for a newly incorporated entity in this sector when applying for regulated activities, public contracts, port access, tax registrations, banking facilities, subsidies, or licenses. This is a risk assessment rather than an official statistical rate. The likelihood is materially lower for a dormant holding company and materially higher for an operating dredging or public-works contractor.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 20 (subscription), 21 (minimum capital), 22 (paid-up capital), 25-34 (bylaws), 62-89 (SL administration and registration); Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996); Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) for the Sociedad de Formación Sucesiva.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for name certification and the provincial Registro Mercantil of the registered office for inscription; electronic filing via CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (Public Deed of Incorporation), inscribed in the provincial Registro Mercantil and published in the Boletin Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SL requires EUR 3,000 minimum capital fully subscribed and paid-up, evidenced by a bank scrow certificate from a Spanish credit institution; alternatively, the Sociedad de Formación Sucesiva regime (Art. 4.2 LSC as amended by Ley 18/2022) permits EUR 1 founding capital subject to mandatory retention of 20% of annual profits until capital reaches EUR 3,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED BY THE FOUNDING PARTNERS: (1) The share capital of EUR 3,000 is subscribed fully and paid in, and the bank escrow certificate is hereby ratified. (2) The registered office is adopted at Calle Ejemplo 1, 28001 Madrid, Spain. (3) The Sole Administrator, [Full Name], domiciled in Spain, is appointed with all statutory powers. (4) The Administrator is authorized to execute the public deed, obtain the provisional tax number, and effect inscription in the Mercantile Registry; the payment of incorporation taxes and registry expenses is approved. (5) The incorporation of the company as Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under Law 1/2010 is confirmed. This resolution is passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain negative name certification from the Central Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid (online via CIRCE portal or the Colegio de Registradores website)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certificacion negativa de denominacion form requesting three alternative corporate names in priority order; the registry verifies that each proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company; upon approval, obtain the negative name certificate and deliver it to the notary for use in the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE copies of all founding partners
Declaration of corporate purpose (marine dredging, seawall construction, ISIC 4290)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected as reserved or identical, resubmit with revised alternative names; the decision may be appealed before the Direccion General de los Registros y del Notariado within the statutory administrative period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit founding capital into an escrow bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Banco de Espana (bank chosen by founders)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the company in formation (e.g. 'SL en constitucion'); deposit the subscribed capital of EUR 3,000 (or the higher amount stated in the bylaws); obtain a bank certificate confirming the deposit, account holder and exact amount; funds remain blocked until the public deed is executed and may only be released to the administrator after inscription.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE copies of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence, provide source-of-funds statements and proof of identity of all signatories; the certificate will be reissued once the compliance file is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Colegio de Notarios chosen by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the negative name certificate, bank capital deposit certificate and draft bylaws to the notary; all founding shareholders (or their electronic proxies) appear before the notary and sign the Escritura de Constitucion; the notary verifies legal aptitude of the founders, expresses the grantors' consent, and immediately submits the deed for provisional NIF filing at the Agencia Tributaria.
required_dossiers: Draft deed and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects or capacity issues, amend the draft and re-execute the deed; for non-residents without NIE, obtain the NIE certificate beforehand from the nearest Spanish consulate or the CNP police station.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the provisional tax identification number (NIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administracion Tributaria (AEAT), local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary presents the first copy of the deed and Form 036 electronically to the AEAT; the provisional NIF for the company in formation is issued immediately, beginning with the letter corresponding to a legal entity; this NIF is used for tax filings, bank account opening and the registry inscription process.
required_dossiers: Notarized first copy of the public deed
Form 036 (declaracion censal) signed by the administrator
Power of attorney if the administrator acts through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT queries the deed, obtain a certified copy from the notary and re-file Form 036 with the requested corrections within the statutory term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the company in the provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil of the province of the registered office (e.g. Registro Mercantil de Madrid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an authenticated copy of the public deed within one month of execution; pay the regulated registry tariff calculated on the share capital; the registrar reviews the legal validity of the incorporation under Article 32 Ley de Sociedades de Capital and issues the inscription certificate, which confers full legal personality.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of the registry tariff
Form of representation if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A suspension or nota de defectos from the registrar must be cured by presenting a rectification deed (escritura de subsanacion) that resolves each defect item, then resubmitting the deed for a second calificacion within the granted period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish incorporation in BORME and obtain the definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Boletin Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME) and Agencia Estatal de Administracion Tributaria (AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Mercantile Registry forwards the incorporated company particulars (capital, registered office, administrator, object) to BORME for publication; simultaneously, submit the registry inscription certificate to the AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF for the fully constituted company.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If BORME publication is delayed, request the registry to expedite the calificacion; if the definitive NIF is delayed, present the inscription certificate to the AEAT and obtain a written confirmation of the definitive NIF assignment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax census, social security registration and municipal activity licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administracion Tributaria (AEAT), Tesoreria General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and the competent Ayuntamiento
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the definitive Form 036 to update the empresario census; register the company as an employer with the TGSS and obtain a Codigo de Cuenta de Cotizacion; adopt and file the occupational risk prevention plan; apply for the municipal Licencia de apertura y actividad for any land or port premises used in the dredging operations.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title for the operating premises
Municipal license application with project description and safety plans
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal license is refused, file alegaciones or an administrative appeal under Ley 7/1985; for technical safety or fire-protection objections, remedy the deficiencies in the project and resubmit for reconsideration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direccion General de la Marina Mercante and Puertos del Estado under the Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility; the port concession or works authorization is issued by the respective Autoridad Portuaria.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorizacion de dragado y vertido al mar de materiales (Dredging and Marine Dumping Authorization), including the port concession/authorization for maritime works and the Licencia de obra required by the Port Authority for seawall and breakwater construction.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transicion Ecologica y el Reto Demografico (Direccion General de Calidad y Evaluacion Ambiental)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full ordinary Environmental Impact Assessment (Evaluacion de Impacto Ambiental Ordinaria) under Ley 21/2013, Annex I item 8(g) for sand and gravel extraction and Annex II item 7(e) for maritime defense works, requiring an EIA study, public information period and favorable environmental authorization before dredging begins.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Real Decreto 817/2015 on environmental quality standards in the aquatic environment; dredged material characterization and dumping authorization per Real Decreto 258/1989; suspended solids and turbidity limits in the designated discharge zone; waste classification and handling per Ley 7/2022; diesel engine emission controls per MARPOL Annex VI and VOC limits under Real Decreto 117/2003.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the competent fire protection service in accordance with the Codigo Tecnico de la Edificacion and Real Decreto 513/2017 on fire protection installations; structural load inspection certificate (Inspeccion Tecnica de Edificios) for storage and plant areas; occupational health and safety clearance under Ley 31/1995 requiring an approved Plan de Prevencion de Riesgos Laborales before works start; port facility security clearance under the ISPS Code for all personnel and equipment entering restricted port zones.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the AEAT Sede Electrónica for tax registration, tax identification number administration, VAT filings, customs procedures, and electronic tax communications. Certain regional authorities administer taxes devolved to Spain's autonomous communities, but national corporate income tax, VAT, and customs administration generally remains with the AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a Spanish Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF), generally consisting of the legal-person identifier letter and seven digits plus a control character. The incorporation workflow is: (1) obtain the company name certificate from the Central Commercial Registry; (2) execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary; (3) obtain a provisional NIF by filing AEAT Form 036 with the deed or incorporation documentation and the required identification of directors, shareholders, and tax representative where applicable; (4) register the company with the competent Commercial Registry; (5) file the registered deed or equivalent evidence with the AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF; and (6) register the relevant business activities and VAT obligations through Form 036 before commencing taxable operations. A foreign shareholder or director generally requires a Spanish Número de Identidad de Extranjero (NIE) or, where applicable, a foreign-person NIF. A non-resident foreign entity conducting taxable activities in Spain must generally apply for a Spanish NIF through Form 036 and may need to appoint a Spanish tax representative where required by Spanish VAT rules, EU status, or the applicable tax treaty. The Spanish VAT identification number is the NIF prefixed by ES and is used for intra-EU transactions and VIES validation. Separate EORI registration is required for customs activity, including imports and exports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish corporate income tax as a separate legal entity and has no general United States-style check-the-box election to elect transparent or disregarded treatment. Limited statutory regimes and elections may apply, including tax consolidation for qualifying Spanish tax groups, the special regime for qualifying newly established companies, the Canary Islands Special Zone where eligibility requirements are satisfied, special regimes for qualifying holding companies or other regulated entities, and voluntary VAT regimes such as the monthly refund regime, the special cash-accounting regime, or VAT group treatment where statutory conditions are met. Spanish and EU anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement ATAD principles and can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or restrict relief for hybrid arrangements; they do not provide a general hybrid classification election for an SL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), supplemented by EU customs and VAT rules. Spain has no general sales-and-use-tax system for mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands; the Canary Islands apply the separate Impuesto General Indirecto Canario (IGIC), and Ceuta and Melilla apply distinct indirect tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold applies for Spanish VAT registration. A person or entity must register before commencing, or when intending to commence, taxable business activities, acquisitions, imports, or supplies requiring a Spanish VAT identity. The small-business exemption threshold applicable in some EU jurisdictions does not operate as a general Spanish domestic VAT-registration threshold. A separate EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold may apply to certain intra-EU consumer distance sales and specified electronically supplied, telecommunications, broadcasting, or electronic services, subject to the applicable OSS rules; it does not replace general Spanish registration obligations for a Spanish SL. Spanish construction, dredging, EPC, and infrastructure activities require transaction-by-transaction analysis of the place-of-supply rules, customer status, immovable-property connection, and any domestic reverse-charge rule.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system for all taxpayers. Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including entities with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, entities within the REDEME monthly refund regime, and voluntary participants, to transmit specified invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT generally within four calendar days, or eight calendar days where an invoice is issued by a third party or the recipient. Electronic invoicing is required in specified public-sector procurement through the FACe infrastructure and is subject to public-procurement invoice rules. The Law on the Creation and Growth of Companies provides for expansion of mandatory B2B electronic invoicing, but implementation depends on the enabling regulations and statutory transition periods; it should not be treated as a presently universal real-time clearance mandate without checking the applicable effective date. The VERI*FACTU invoicing-system requirements introduce standardized integrity, traceability, and anti-manipulation controls for qualifying invoicing systems, subject to the applicable implementation timetable. Spain has no general VAT digital-stamp requirement for ordinary invoices, although invoices must satisfy formal content, authenticity, integrity, legibility, and retention requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, the Spanish VAT exemption with the right to deduct generally applies where goods are dispatched or transported from mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands to a destination outside the EU customs territory, and the supplier retains objective evidence of export and exit from the EU. The export declaration, transport evidence, commercial documents, and customs exit confirmation must be consistent with the invoice and transaction. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for exemption with the right to deduct where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and required reporting and evidence conditions are satisfied. Services supplied to a business established outside Spain may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the general B2B place-of-supply rule, rather than technically zero-rated. Services connected with immovable property, including many construction, breakwater, civil-engineering, and dredging works, are generally taxed where the immovable property is located; offshore performance, customer location, vessel status, and the precise contractual scope must therefore be analyzed. A maritime seawall or breakwater project located in Spain will generally not qualify as an export merely because the customer is foreign or payment is received from abroad. VAT refunds require valid purchase invoices, deductible business use, proper VAT books and filings, and evidence supporting any export or exempt transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration or Single Administrative Document equivalent, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN), commodity classification, customs procedure, exporter, consignee, value, and transport information
Customs decision or electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory, such as the Export Accompanying Document or equivalent exit-results record
Commercial invoice, contract or purchase order, packing list where applicable, and transport documentation such as bill of lading, sea waybill, CMR, or air waybill
Evidence linking the exported goods to the Spanish supplier's VAT invoice and accounting records
Proof of delivery or destination evidence where necessary to establish the transport chain and resolve customs or VAT discrepancies
Import or destination-country customs evidence where available and relevant

Bank payment or inward-remittance evidence may support audit substantiation and anti-money-laundering controls but is not, by itself, a universal statutory condition for Spanish VAT export exemption and does not replace customs proof of exit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days for export proceeds. Export proceeds may generally remain abroad, subject to banking, anti-money-laundering, accounting, customs, transfer-pricing, and reporting obligations. If an export exemption or other VAT relief is unsupported, the AEAT may assess the unpaid VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and applicable penalties, together with correction of VAT deductions and related tax filings. Ordinary underpayment penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax depending on the seriousness, concealment, repeated conduct, or fraud indicators; the precise penalty depends on the breached provision and facts. False, manipulated, or inconsistent customs evidence can also trigger customs debt, import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture measures, and administrative sanctions under EU and Spanish customs law. Deliberate fraudulent conduct may create criminal tax exposure where statutory thresholds and intent requirements are met. Voluntary correction before notification of an audit may reduce exposure under the Spanish General Tax Law, but documentary deficiencies cannot be cured solely by later bank remittance or retroactive invoicing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem and in coordination with the European Central Bank; Spanish foreign exchange oversight is otherwise administered under EU Capital Movements Regulation and the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies the EU Treaty principle of free movement of capital and payments. The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There are no exchange permits for capital contributions, profit remittances, loan repayments, or trade settlements. Non-resident investors may freely repatriate dividends and liquidation proceeds, subject only to standard corporate income tax, withholding tax where applicable, and the submission of annual or statistical declarations to the Banco de España for amounts above EUR 50,000 or €100,000 thresholds. No dividend blockage or repatriation licensing exists. The sole practical hurdles concern banking compliance, anti-money-laundering documentation, and accurate classification of the payment purpose code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation in Spain to surrender foreign-currency export proceeds or to convert them into euros. Export invoices may be issued in EUR or foreign currency; however, Spanish electronic invoicing and customs rules require accurate declaration of export receipts and, when payments are received in foreign currency, the underlying commercial documents must match the foreign exchange reference. For amounts exceeding statutory thresholds, exporters must report foreign-currency balances to the Banco de España for statistical balance-of-payments purposes. No mandatory conversion ratio or timing deadline exists because the euro is the domestic currency and the regime permits exporters to hold foreign currency accounts with Spanish banks, subject only to general reporting duties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with substantial legal constraints. A Spanish-registered fintech or electronic money institution (EMI) supervised by the Banco de España may provide IBAN accounts, payment initiation, and currency conversion services. Cross-border foreign fintechs operating under EU payment services passports can serve Spanish corporate clients on a branch or agent basis, but Spanish AML/KYC rules generally require the underlying corporate entity, its directors, and beneficial owners to complete enhanced due diligence before an operational account is opened. Pure offshore digital EMIs without a Spanish or EU-authorised passport are not viable for receiving capital escrow funds or supporting treasury flows because they cannot guarantee segregated client funds, Spanish tax identification (NIF), or reliable access to SWIFT and SEPA clearing. For an ISIC 4290 dredging EPC company, a bank-backed EMI may be used as a secondary collection rail, but the primary operating account should be held at a fully licensed Spanish credit institution to meet Port Authority milestone payment requirements and counterparty bank KYC expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, physical presence of at least one duly authorised director or legal representative is normally required during the initial onboarding interview at the branch or through a bank-approved notarial video conference. Spanish banks increasingly accept remote identification only when the identity is verified by a notary public, a Spanish consular official, or an authorised electronic trust services provider (eIDAS-certified video KYC). Each ultimate beneficial owner and every director with signatory authority must present a valid national identity document or passport, Spanish tax identification number (NIE/NIF), and proof of address. Signature specimens must be notarised. In practice, a first board meeting in Spain, combined with notarised powers of attorney, will satisfy the physical-presence mandate; pure remote account opening without any Spanish nexus is normally rejected by tier-1 Spanish banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a non-resident corporate entity registered in a jurisdiction considered non-cooperative or blacklisted by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) or Spanish regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an independent corporate extract and certificate of good standing from the beneficial owner's commercial registry; detailed organisational chart tracing all intermediate entities; notarised and apostilled identification documents of all UBOs; audited financial statements for the last two years; declaration of source of wealth and source of funds; Spanish anti-money-laundering form of beneficial ownership (BOR); and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the structure, accompanied by evidence of the direct link to the dredging project tender and the Port Authority contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected inbound capital contribution or initial escrow deposit has no clear purpose or references a sensitive origin-country jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the executed shareholders' resolution for the capital contribution; notarised capital increase agreement; bank-issued certified draft or SWIFT MT103 with purpose code

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) — balance sheet, profit and loss account, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows, notes to the accounts, auditor's report (when applicable) — approved by the shareholders' general meeting and deposited at the Mercantile Registry together with the annual beneficial-ownership confirmation (declaración anual de titularidad real).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered-office province; coordinated by the Registro Mercantil Central under the Ministry of Justice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The general meeting must approve the accounts within 6 months of the fiscal year end (by June 30 for a calendar-year company); deposit at the Mercantile Registry must be made within 1 month of approval (by July 30 for calendar-year companies).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted deposit triggers 'cierre registral': no further registration or filing is admitted for the company until the annual accounts are deposited; ICAC and Mercantile Registry fines of EUR 200–EUR 12,000 for late filing, rising to EUR 60,000 for continued non-filing; company directors incur personal liability for resulting damages.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created entities deriving qualifying business income for the first two taxable years with positive corporate tax base; 30% special regime for entities taxed under the Spanish territorial scope in Ceuta and Melilla for offshore activities; tax credits for R&D and technological innovation; digital economy/general deductions may apply but no statutory holiday for maritime dredging; 4% reinvestment tax credit in certain cases under Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (LIS) provisions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed via Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic filing portal, with mandatory presentation using qualified electronic certificate; accompanying Modelo 405 for non-resident entities without permanent establishment is not the operative corporate return but Modelo 200 is the annual corporate income tax return for an SL resident in Spain.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December year-end, filing deadline is July 25 of the following year; if the deadline falls on a non-business day, it shifts to the next immediate business day); advance payments via Modelo 217 are quarterly (April 20, October 20, December 20) under the installment-payment mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (NIF), corporate name, and tax domicile of the SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Spanish NIF of the entity; non-resident shareholders are not reflected in this field; a non-resident owner with a Spanish permanent establishment must report the branch attribution separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period start and end dates; must coincide with the civil exercise unless a corporate event triggers an abbreviated period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact period of Spanish tax residence; a non-resident entity with a permanent establishment in Spain files for the full period of activity of that permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax adjusted for permanent differences, temporary differences including depreciation, provisions, and tax-exempt items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the taxable base from Spanish-source income attributable to the permanent establishment; expenses incurred outside Spain are deductible only when properly linked to the permanent establishment's activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic double taxation relief, international double taxation relief, tax credits for R&D, export activities, and reinvestment of nondistributed profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief by entering the corresponding credit under international double taxation; for non-resident shareholders receiving dividends, the credit is not claimed in this box because withholding applies at shareholder level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax at 25% on taxable base, reduced after credits and prepayments to produce the final tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the final quota for the Spanish permanent establishment; no offset is allowed for taxes paid abroad on profits not attributable to Spanish PE activities except under treaty credit provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments (Modelo 217) and withholdings from Spanish customers on invoicing applicable to construction and similar services; at least 1% retention applies to works projects, increased to 2% in certain cases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reflect Spanish withholding certificates and AEAT payment receipts for the fiscal year; maritime dredging contracts with public authorities commonly trigger the special 2% retention on construction works if treated as construction contracts under Article 101 of the Personal Income Tax Regulation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due or refundable after deducting all prepayments from the total liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The differential quota may be reduced if the PE has paid excessive retentions; no additional tax relief arises from the shareholder's non-resident status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Domicilio fiscal, representante, otorgamiento de poder)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal representative in Spain and signed power to represent the taxpayer before AEAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory designation of a Spanish resident individual or legal entity representative when the SL is controlled by non-resident directors and has no effective Spanish management; the representative must be vested with sufficient authority for filing and audit procedures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 1% of the amount due per month of delay, up to 15% if filed spontaneously after the statutory deadline; if filed after AEAT notice, surcharge increases to 10% to 20% plus late-payment interest; failure to file without liquidation results in a minimum penalty of EUR 300 and maximum of 20% of the omitted amount; inaccuracies with criminal intent can elevate fines to 150% of the tax amount; late payment interest at the legal rate (currently approximately 3.75% annually, adjusted in the Spanish State Budget Act).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividend distributions paid by a Spanish resident entity to non-resident shareholders, absent domestic exemption or treaty relief; domestic withholding rate applied by the payer when distributing profits; refund mechanism available where treaty rate is lower.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the applicable double taxation agreement (notably the Spain-Netherlands, Spain-Luxembourg, Spain-Germany, or Spain-UAE treaty depending on shareholder residence), the beneficial owner must: obtain a Spanish NIF for the non-resident entity; submit the Spanish form 210 for non-resident income along with the annual form 216 (quarterly withholding summary) and form 296 (annual informative return) if the payer has applied withholding; secure from the residence-country tax authority a certificate of tax residence (TRC) stating the shareholder's treaty residency and beneficial ownership; deliver the TRC to the Spanish paying agent before distribution, or alternatively request a refund through the non-resident procedure according to the rules of the General Tax Law and Royal Decree 1065/2007; AEAT may require a certified Spanish translation and apostille/Hague Convention legalization if from a non-EU state.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding rate of 24% for Spanish-source royalties paid to non-residents, reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive when the recipient is an EU parent or associated company satisfying the 25% ownership threshold and subject to EU corporate tax without exemption; under typical Spanish tax treaties with OECD counterparts the royalty rate is usually 10-15%, and under the Spain-Netherlands treaty 10%. Interest: statutory withholding rate of 19% on interest paid to non-residents, generally reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, and to around 10-12% under many tax treaties; the Spain-Netherlands treaty provides 10% on interest; domestic exemption applies in certain cases to government and intra-EU corporate interest; documentary requirements mirror those for dividends: TRC, form 210, and declaration of beneficial ownership; failure to apply the correct reduced rate exposes the payer to substitute responsibility for the omitted withholding plus interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 of annual net revenues for entities required to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File) under article 18 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law and Royal Decree 634/2015; Master File obligations apply when the group's consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 75 million; a simplified local file may be required when the entity is a constituent of a multinational group with Spanish operations and the related-party transaction value exceeds EUR 250,000, subject to the AEAT annual tax transparency form (Modelo 232) threshold of EUR 250,000 per related-party transaction type falling under the documentation regime.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spanish law does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as a distinct statute, but the substantive equivalent operates through the anti-abuse and substance-over-form doctrine: the general anti-abuse rule in Article 15 of the General Tax Law (LGT) permits recharacterisation of sham transactions; case law and AEAT practice require that an entity have premises, personnel, equipment, and effective management in Spain to be considered tax-resident and to avoid the lifting of limited liability; the corporate income tax residence test (Article 8 LIS) looks to incorporation under domestic law, registered office, or place of effective management; a dredging EPC company performing works through mobile maritime vessels must demonstrate Spanish establishment via vessel registry, local contracting office, and project management substance; failure of substance can trigger assessment on the actual beneficial owner, 150% penalty on the alleged improper deduction, and criminal referral under tax evasion rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mistakenly booking dredging revenue in low-tax jurisdictions or concealing Spanish-source maritime contracts performed in Spanish territorial waters; failure to declare revenue from public works concessions or port authority milestone payments; deliberate omission or false invoices in the sludge/sand transport chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of 50% to 150% of the omitted tax amount under Article 191 LGT; for amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 per fiscal year, criminal tax fraud under Organic Law 10/1995 Article 305 carries imprisonment of 1 to 5 years; increasing to 2 to 6 years when fraud exceeds EUR 600,000 or uses shell entities that hamper collection; criminal penalty includes a fine of up to 6 times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax under Article 43.2 LGT when responsible for the omission or for failure to wind up the company after dissolution; criminal liability extends to the de facto manager (gestor de hecho); travel bans, passport surrender, and preventive seizure of maritime vessels may be imposed; conviction carries disqualification from public funding and port concessions; civil restitution of the defrauded amount plus late-payment interest is ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length intercompany rates for dredging vessel chartering, fuel supply, crew services, engineering services, or equipment leasing from a foreign related party; failing to file Modelo 232 or to develop contemporaneous documentation; omitting a profit attribution to the Spanish entity for the EPC margin while delegating procurement and vessel operation to a tax-haven related entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of a price adjustment to the arm's-length result plus late-payment interest; penalty of 25% on the hidden tax base for unassessed related-party transactions in the hands of the Spanish entity where documentation is absent or incomplete; incorrect documentation may attract a EUR 15,000 fixed penalty per omitted item up to a maximum of EUR 150,000, and non-submission of Modelo 232 incurs penalties of EUR 100 per data item with a minimum of EUR 1,200 and maximum of EUR 10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false transfer pricing documentation or knowingly signed non-arm's-length agreements are severally liable for the adjustment and penalty; audit exposure includes criminal referral for fraudulent falsehood where documentation is used to mislead tax authorities, with imprisonment from 1 to 5 years; the maritime dredging sector's heavy capital costs generate scrutiny of freight and hire charges, thus requiring vessel charter documentation, time-charter comparables, and crew cost analyses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an SL that has no real office, no locally engaged engineers, no procurement activity in Spain, and whose only role is the final signing of port authority contracts while actual dredging subcontractors are related foreign vehicles; use of a letterbox entity to channelfunds without staff, vessel, or decision-making in Spanish territory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT and Spanish Land Registry courts may pierce the corporate veil under the doctrine of fraudulent incorporation; the company may be reclassified as a transparent entity, with tax assessed on the non-resident shareholder or actual beneficiary; administrative fine for abuse of legal form under Article 15 LGT up to 150% of the tax evaded; courts may order the monetary sanction of committing insolvency-motive dissolution and loss of the NIF for active operations; if the structure triggers anti-money-laundering examination for unexplained vessel ownership, penalties of EUR 1,500 to EUR 300,000 under the Spanish AML Law (10/2010) apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual administrators, shadow directors and beneficial owners are jointly liable for the corporate tax of the SL when the company is unable to pay after being declared insolvent and the non-exercise of substance constitutes an aggravating circumstance; travel bans imposed by criminal courts if the vessel arbitration or port statutes are circumvented through shell companies; imprisonment up to 4 years for wrongdoing in the context of corporate insolvency under the Spanish Criminal Code; directors are disqualified from managing a Spanish company for up to 2 years in the event of abuse of the corporate entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership registry for high-value maritime contracts, misrepresenting the true owner of dredging vessels through bearer instruments or nominee arrangements, falsifying freight contracts in NFTS or fuel invoices to launder proceeds; refusing to provide port authority statements for the execution of a public works concession.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Copyright to the Spanish AML supervisor SEPBLAC: disciplinary fines of EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 for law-incident breaches under Law 10/2010; criminal laundering sanctions under Article 301-304 Criminal Code: imprisonment 6 months to 6 years plus fine of 1 to 6 times the laundered value; professional exclusion from public contracting for up to 2 years, cancellation of the dredging permit and exclusion from state procurement lists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company directors whose vessel and cash flows replicate money-laundering typologies may face preventive arrest in satisfaction of bail for overseas flight risk, seizure of the sea-going vessels as instrumental goods in the crime, and civil compensation plus procedural costs; the maritime property registries are flagged for freezing orders, and directors may lose all limited liability exemption as LGT Article 42 imposes subsidiary responsibility for penal debts arising in the exercise of corporate management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure of an SL to file Modelo 200, Modelo 216/220 quarterly withholding forms, or Modelo 217 advance payments on schedule; failure to withhold the Spanish income tax on dividends, interest or royalties paid to non-resident shareholders or creditors; intentionally not withholding when the owner is a Luxembourg or Dutch holding vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 192 LGT: fine of 50% to 150% of the unwithheld amount for the nonresident income tax; late filing of declarations without self-assessment: fixed penalty of EUR 200 plus a proportional penalty of 20% of the amount not paid; late filing of Modelo 200 after AEAT has served a prior notice results in a EUR 1,000 minimum penalty; interest from the date the amount should have been entered; criminal sanctions if unwithheld amount fraud exceeds EUR 120,000 in a single year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly refrain from applying the Spanish withholding at 19% when declaring dividends to a non-resident shareholder are personally liable for the entire withheld quota plus penalty; if criminal liability arises, the company's administration body can be jointly sanctioned and the director may be prohibited from being a director of any Spanish company; Portuguese and EU arrest warrants serve as travel bans, and Spanish maritime firms risk forfeiture of the vessel as a means of payment for criminal fines.
